Pharmacy Benefit Managers (PBMs) are under fire for practices that inflate drug costs and harm patient care. Critics expose how PBMs claim to save payers $1,040 annually per person, but the reality is far from it. Spread pricing, rebate manipulation, and anti-competitive steering are just a few tactics PBMs use to line their pockets while independent pharmacies struggle. 

Patients suffer as 29% ration medications due to costs, and PBMs override doctor-preferred treatments. Legislative efforts aim to dismantle this corrupt system, but Big Pharma's resistance is fierce. 

It's time to end this charade and put patients first.
